summary: Iteration 10 backend + frontend testing complete. 21/21 pytest backend tests pass (100%). All review-request items verified. Stripe checkout correctly returns 503 'Stripe not configured' (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY placeholder). IP-based anti-trial-abuse confirmed: second registration from same X-Forwarded-For rejected with 400. Admin (isaac@timestables.ca / admin12345) returns is_admin=true + role=admin + has_access=true. /api/admin/stats returns all required fields with signups_30d/revenue_30d length=31; non-admin gets 403; unauth gets 401. /api/admin/users?q=isaac returns Isaac. PUT /api/admin/cms persists and /api/cms/public reflects change. Frontend: guest sees brand+Sign-in only (all nav-* testids absent), admin login shows nav-admin + amber hud-user pill, /admin renders admin-dashboard with stat-users/stat-subs/stat-mrr/stat-revenue tiles + signups-chart + revenue-chart + recent-payments, Users tab search returns Isaac, CMS tab saves and shows 'Saved' toast which propagates to Home hero-title, regular user sees nav-learn/daily/stats/shop/settings but NOT nav-admin, regular user visiting /admin redirects to /, /play/long-div still renders Long Division (With Remainder section), brand 'Times Tables.ca' present.
critical_code_review_comments: Review-request mentioned nav-play testid but Layout.jsx:46 uses testid='nav-home' for the Play link. Cosmetic — consider renaming to nav-play to match the visible label and reduce confusion for future tests.

register() rejects a *second non-admin* signup from the same IP, but the admin role is excluded from the check (line 268 `role: {$ne:'admin'}`). That is by design, but note: If a real user ever gets an 'admin' role bump, their household could register another trial. Acceptable.

stripe_webhook (server.py:509) only verifies Stripe-Signature if STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set; with blank secret it falls back to json.loads(payload). Dev-friendly, but unsafe for prod — guard with an env flag before deploy.

server.py /api/stripe/checkout creates the session BEFORE writing the payment_transactions row; if the DB insert fails after Stripe creates the session the user has a dangling Stripe checkout. Consider wrapping in a try/except that cancels the Stripe session on insert failure, or record tx before calling Stripe.
admin_stats (server.py:541) streams all paid payment_transactions into memory to compute totals — fine today, but will not scale; add a $match date filter + $group aggregation when row count grows.
